$comment: Single source of truth for the HTTP response headers every Fly GACA front serves.
Production is Google Cloud: a Cloud Storage backend bucket (the SPA) and a Cloud Run
backend service (the API), both behind one HTTPS load balancer. GCP applies custom
response headers per BACKEND, not per path, so the split here is deliberate:
security  -> identical on every response; emitted as --custom-response-headers by
scripts/lib/headers.mjs and applied with `gcloud compute backend-buckets
cache     -> per path, so it CANNOT be a backend header. Set as Cloud Storage object
metadata at upload time by scripts/deploy-web.mjs.
vercel.json and netlify.toml are dormant mirrors and firebase.json is the live Firebase
Hosting front; none may rot: tests/headers-parity.test.ts fails the build when any of
them (or public/_headers) drifts from this file.
script-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' deliberately: index.html ships two inline scripts by
design (the no-flash theme init and the app-shell remover), and both propagate into
every prerendered snapshot. Replacing it with static sha256 hashes is possible but
needs a build-time stamping step across all header copies; until then removing it
would break every page. style-src needs it for framer-motion's inline styles and the

security.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.moyasar.com https://www.googletagmanager.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.moyasar.com; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://*.googleusercontent.com https://cdn.moyasar.com https://www.googletagmanager.com https://storage.googleapis.com; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.moyasar.com https://www.google-analytics.com https://analytics.google.com https://region1.google-analytics.com https://firebase.googleapis.com https://firebaseinstallations.googleapis.com https://storage.googleapis.com; frame-src 'self' https://api.moyasar.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests

cache.why: The service worker must be revalidated every load or a stale one pins users to an old build forever.

index.html names the hashed entry chunks. Cache it and a deploy is invisible until the TTL expires. Vercel and Netlify serve the SPA fallback themselves and declare no rule, so the mirrors map to null.
Vite content-hashes every filename here, so a changed file is a changed URL.
The regulatory corpus changes on a sync cadence, not per deploy; the SW serves it network-first.
